Opaque

/oh-PAYK/ — rhymes with wake, stake · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something that is opaque cannot be seen through because light does not pass through it clearly.

The bathroom's opaque glass lets in light but no prying eyes.

Worked Example

The company's opaque hiring process left applicants with no visibility into how decisions were made.

Opaque emphasizes that something cannot be seen through—literally, light does not pass. It's more precise than 'secretive' because opaque describes a physical property of blocking light, not a deliberate choice to hide information.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unclear: Unclear describes information that is hard to follow — an unclear explanation muddles the mind. Opaque is physical: an opaque material blocks light so completely that nothing behind it can be seen. A lecture can be unclear; a painted-over window is opaque. One clouds meaning, the other blocks vision.

cloudy: Cloudy means murky the way stirred-up water or a hazy sky is murky — you can still half-see through it, just poorly. Opaque goes all the way: no light passes, so nothing behind it shows at all. Cloudy dims the view; opaque removes it.

secretive: Secretive describes people and organizations that deliberately keep their inner workings hidden — a choice, not a material. Opaque names a physical property: a substance light cannot pass through. A committee can be secretive about its plans; the frosted glass on its office door is merely opaque.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

transparent: letting light and meaning pass straight through

lucid: so clear it is instantly understood

Where it sits · how completely it blocks things out — translucent → opaque → impenetrable → sealed

translucent vs. opaque: Translucent is weaker than opaque — translucent glass still lets light glow through, while opaque material blocks the view entirely.

impenetrable vs. opaque: Impenetrable is stronger than opaque: an opaque report is hard to see into, but an impenetrable one resists every attempt to get through it.

sealed vs. opaque: Sealed is the extreme end beyond opaque — something opaque merely hides its contents from view, while something sealed is shut off completely, letting nothing in or out.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — opaque

Root — opaque: shaded, dark (Latin opacus, whose deeper origin is unknown) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Opaque comes whole from Latin opacus, 'shaded, dark' — a shaded thing lets no light through, which grew into today's meaning of material (or writing) you cannot see into.

Use the root in a new word: opacity

Use the root in a new word: opacity: Scientists measured the opacity of the pond water to see how much light it blocked — opacity is simply the noun form of opaque.

Word Building

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Opaque is precise when describing materials or substances that block light and vision. Unlike 'unclear' (information that's confusing), opaque specifically refers to physical properties. Use it for glass, fabric, paint, and other tangible things, not for behavior or communication.
